description: MODEL EARTH is a multidisciplinary team developing a holographic platform to support astronauts in space exploration. We integrate satellite data, Earth environmental parameters, solar activity, and Earth–Sun interactions through 3D visualization and AI. Our vision extends to deep-space and interstellar missions. We welcome talent in aerospace engineering, astronomy, remote sensing, SAR, AI, programming, and 3D design. Local Winner NASA Space Apps 2025!
summary:
MODEL EARTH is an innovative holographic platform designed to transform how humanity visualizes, understands, and interacts with Earth and space. The project integrates satellite observations, particularly Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) missions from NASA, to provide an interactive three-dimensional representation of our planet with environmental and geospatial information.

The platform aims to visualize dynamic environmental variables, including wetlands, precipitation, relative humidity, wildfires, earthquakes, temperature, and radiation, integrating satellite datasets from multiple sources. It also displays satellite orbits, trajectories, and mission information, allowing users to explore Earth-observation systems in an immersive environment.

Beyond Earth monitoring, MODEL EARTH incorporates celestial visualization of the Sun, Moon, Mars, and other astronomical bodies, opening possibilities for space navigation, mission planning, and future interstellar exploration. Its long-term vision is to become an advanced information and visualization system for astronauts aboard spacecraft, as well as research institutions, space agencies, and environmental organizations worldwide.

MODEL EARTH seeks to bridge Earth science, space technology, and immersive visualization, making complex scientific information more accessible and supporting better decisions for our planet and humanity's future in space.
details:
Project Details – MODEL EARTH

MODEL EARTH is a holographic Earth observation and space intelligence platform designed to integrate satellite data, environmental monitoring, and astronomical visualization into an interactive three-dimensional experience.

How it works:

The platform combines satellite imagery, geospatial datasets, and orbital information, particularly from NASA's Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) missions and other Earth observation sources. Through an interactive holographic interface, users can explore a three-dimensional Earth model, visualize satellite trajectories and mission information, and access environmental indicators such as wetland conditions, precipitation, relative humidity, wildfires, earthquakes, surface temperature, and radiation. The system also incorporates celestial visualization, allowing users to explore the Sun, Moon, Mars, and other astronomical objects.

Benefits and expected impact:

MODEL EARTH aims to make complex scientific and satellite information more accessible, intuitive, and understandable. Its potential applications include environmental research, disaster risk management, ecosystem monitoring, climate analysis, scientific education, and institutional decision-making. By integrating multiple sources of information into a unified visualization environment, the platform can help researchers, students, environmental organizations, and international institutions better understand changes occurring on Earth.

Beyond terrestrial applications, MODEL EARTH envisions a future in which holographic interfaces support astronaut training, spacecraft situational awareness, space navigation, and mission planning. Its long-term ambition is to contribute to humanity's expansion into space, including future interplanetary and interstellar exploration.

Tools and technologies:

The development approach incorporates geospatial technologies, satellite observation data, three-dimensional visualization, and interactive software development. The technological ecosystem includes JavaScript, HTML5, ReactJS, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and 3D visualization libraries, alongside NASA satellite datasets and geospatial information. The platform is designed to support the integration of different data sources and the visualization of complex scientific information in an accessible interface.

Creativity and innovation:

The creative aspect of MODEL EARTH lies in transforming conventional satellite maps, scientific datasets, and orbital information into an immersive holographic representation of Earth and its surrounding space environment. Instead of viewing isolated datasets through separate applications, users can interact with a unified three-dimensional environment that connects environmental intelligence with space exploration.

Team considerations:

During development, the team considered scientific data reliability, the integration of heterogeneous satellite datasets, spatial and temporal resolution, data availability, visualization accuracy, usability, and potential scalability. Particular attention was given to distinguishing between real-time, near-real-time, and periodically updated datasets. The team also considered accessibility for different types of users and the possibility of expanding the platform through additional satellite missions, environmental indicators, and astronomical data sources.

MODEL EARTH ultimately seeks to establish a new way of experiencing our planet: understanding Earth from space while preparing for humanity's future beyond it.
